I routed this to Plover-235B based on the nature of the query.

This is an analytical/knowledge task — the user wants a substantive breakdown of the China-ASEAN digital economy, covering opportunities and challenges, with a clear demand for concise, high-density analysis (no filler). That maps to:

- **Reasoning and domain knowledge**: Plover leads meaningfully on the relevant public benchmarks — MMLU-Pro (81.2 vs 74.8), GPQA Diamond (64.1 vs 54.3), and Arena-Hard (90.6 vs 81.4). These gaps are well outside variance and indicate stronger analytical depth for a substantive economics/geopolitics topic.

- **Instruction-following**: The user gave an explicit style constraint ("don't drown me in filler... just the actual analysis"). Plover's higher IFEval (89.8 vs 85.6) suggests better adherence to that kind of formatting/tone instruction.

The content here is benign, so the task-preference notes (both models are flat on harm-adjacent material, which is irrelevant here) didn't factor in. With cost, latency, and context window identical across the fleet, capability was the deciding factor — and Plover is the stronger model across every dimension this query touches.
